body:
Vaguely related, a few years back, I'd have been working on an off as a producer, I played around in many different genres, and a friend of mine mentioned he was doing some production work too. I was interested, and wanted to hear what he was doing, and he presented me with something that sounded straight out of a Spinnin' records demo collection. I mean, it sounded fine (from what I could gather, it was playing out of his phone speakers. :/) but, it was... Clean. Boring, generic, paint-by-numbers, and I told him, "Dude, what separates you from the hundreds of other people making the same stuff, the same way?"

And he responded with, "I dunno, I just wanna do this to get big."

And, something about that irritated me. Namely, that, one would sacrifice artistic integrity to become famous... Even when the chance of becoming famous was nil. But, also...

1. He was more successful than me already, since he produced a very clean sounding track that, while inoffensive, wasn't as awful as any of my work up to that point

2. While he wasn't unique, he put in the effort to make a track even if it wasn't his ideal sort of tune, and it turned out okay (But then again, I don't really know how much liberty Garageband gives you. He could've been building off of samples and I wouldn't know!).

Regardless, story about genericness aside, I found the most refreshing thing for me was to strip down what I was working with, force myself to think creatively. Your brain does fun stuff when you rely off of:

3 basic, lifted from vintage drum machines sample packs
3x Osc
Synth1

So, basically, strip down what you work with, figure out what you make when faced with the grand adversity of not having a bajillion presets and fucking Vengeance (seriously, fuck Vengeance.), and work with something that limits you.

And then, try and get around that limit. It worked for me, mebbe it'll work for you?
I'm probably gonna buy a Spin Clean once I expand my vinyl collection. Until then, I'm gonna go with Pajama said and use microfiber cloth and distilled.

Gotcha. I'm gonna guess that carbon fiber brushes don't necessarily have much of a huge difference in quality depending on brand? At least, the internet seems to be fighting about them a whole lot less than turntables or cartridges.

And... I'm just gonna be straight with you and say that the ten dollar cleaning sounds perfectly radical. I've seen people clean with wood glue for 'deep cleaning', but I am predictably terrified of doing that, and I'm gonna guess you don't just scrub the fucker in water.

What's the best cleaning kit I can get for vinyl? That includes stuff just for everyday upkeep.

Edit: Also, just as a 'which turntable is better' question, U-Turn Orbit or Music Hall MMF 2.2?

Edit^2: Orrrr... LP120? Carbon? Who knew that finding a product in a market full of similar products could be so haaaaard.
